title: Majestic Glory
reviewNotes: Reconstructed Rxa4+ to distract the king, the premature pawn push, and queen-versus-rook promotion contrast. Checked actual queen stalemate and the legal Ka3 escape after rook promotion.
transcript: Fools would resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see, white is only two steps away from getting a new queen. But if we push the pawn, this is a big mistake. After rook to b3 check, we either shuffle the king back and forth between a2 and b2, or the moment that we step to c2, there is going to be a fork [music] picking up the pawn. And in this position with a rook and a pawn each, this is going to be a draw. So from the starting position, white has to realize that the only way to fight for an advantage is to play the majestic and brilliant rook takes a4. A beautiful sacrifice. And once [music] the black king takes the rook, now we can push the pawn without worrying about [music] the rook coming to c3 because the king is not supporting that anymore. The pawn is defending d8, so the rook cannot stop the promotion like this. And if black tries to give checks like this, after the king moves and attacks the rook, now again there is going to be no way to come behind the pawn or to the side of it, which means that white is going to be able to promote to a queen and win the game. So is this it? Is white simply out of the woods? Well, not exactly. With rook to b3 check, again. What? We said that the king can just go to c2 and now there is not going to be a fork picking up the pawn. But black doesn't need to take the pawn because after rook to b5, we run [music] into a problem. If we get a queen, this is now actually a blunder because black has the brilliant rook c5. A sacrifice that attacks the queen and the king. So the rook has to be taken, but now this is a stalemate and [music] a draw. But not all is said and done because of course, instead of promoting to a queen, white can promote to a rook. A rare and beautiful under promotion [music] that maintains the advantage because although a rook can often be enough to hold back a pawn and rook after we get a chance to cut out the king on the A file, there is going to be no way to achieve a drawn setup. The king is cut out and white will win this game. Don't forget that you can get the Fool's Will Resign merch from the link in bio.
